# 1 Kings Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame — fame connected with the name of the LORD — and came to test him with difficult questions.

**2** She arrived in Jerusalem with a massive entourage: camels loaded with spices, enormous quantities of gold, and precious stones. When she met Solomon, she posed every question she had prepared.

**3** Solomon answered every one. Nothing was too complex for the king to explain.

**4** When the queen of Sheba saw the full extent of Solomon's wisdom, the palace he had built,

**5** the food on his table, how his officials were seated, how his servants stood at attention in their uniforms, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the LORD's temple — it took her breath away.

**6** She said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom was true.

**7** I didn't believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. In fact, I wasn't told even half of it. Your wisdom and wealth far exceed the reports I heard.

**8** How fortunate your people are! How fortunate these servants of yours, who stand in your presence every day and hear your wisdom!

**9** Praise be to the LORD your God, who has taken such delight in you that he placed you on the throne of Israel. Because the LORD's love for Israel is eternal, he has made you king to uphold justice and righteousness."

**10** She gave the king 120 talents of gold, a huge quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again did such a quantity of spices arrive as what the queen of Sheba gave Solomon.

**11** Hiram's fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought large shipments of almug wood and precious stones.

**12** The king used the almug wood to make railings for the LORD's temple and the royal palace, and lyres and harps for the musicians. No such shipment of almug wood has ever arrived since.

**13** King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted — whatever she asked for — in addition to the royal gifts he gave her from his own generosity. Then she returned home with her attendants.

**14** The weight of gold Solomon received in a single year was 666 talents,

**15** not counting revenue from merchants, traders, all the Arabian kings, and the regional governors.

**16** King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold, using six hundred shekels of gold for each one.

**17** He also made three hundred smaller shields of hammered gold, using three minas of gold for each. He placed them in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.

**18** The king made a great throne inlaid with ivory and overlaid with pure gold.

**19** The throne had six steps, with a rounded back. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing on each side.

**20** Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each end. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.

**21** All of Solomon's drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Nothing was made of silver — silver was considered worthless in Solomon's day.

**22** The king had a fleet of trading ships at sea alongside Hiram's fleet. Every three years the ships returned, loaded with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

**23** King Solomon surpassed every king on earth in wealth and wisdom.

**24** The whole world wanted an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had given him.

**25** Year after year, each visitor brought gifts — silver and gold articles, robes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.

**26** Solomon amassed fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he stationed in chariot cities and with him in Jerusalem.

**27** The king made silver as common as rocks in Jerusalem, and cedar as plentiful as the ordinary sycamore trees in the western foothills.

**28** Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and Kue. The royal traders purchased them from Kue at the going rate.

**29** A chariot from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse one hundred and fifty. They were also exported through Solomon's agents to the Hittite and Aramean kings.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **10:1 — "fame connected with the name of the LORD"**: The queen doesn't come because Solomon is rich. She comes because his fame is linked to his God. The temple has done its job: it has made YHWH internationally famous.

2. **10:5 — "it took her breath away"**: The Hebrew says literally "there was no more spirit in her." This is awe at its most physical — she is literally winded by what she sees. The narrator wants you to feel the overwhelming scale.

3. **10:9 — a pagan queen's theology**: The queen of Sheba delivers the most theologically precise statement about Solomon's reign: God loves Israel, therefore he appointed a king, whose job is justice and righteousness. A foreign queen understands what Solomon himself will forget.

4. **10:14 — 666 talents**: The annual gold income. Whether or not this number was chosen for later symbolic resonance, it represents the peak of human wealth-accumulation — and in the narrative logic of 1 Kings, peaks exist to be fallen from.

5. **10:26-29 — the three violations**: Deuteronomy 17:16-17 forbids three things for Israel's king: multiplying horses (especially from Egypt), multiplying silver and gold, and multiplying wives. By the end of chapter 10, Solomon has violated two of three. Chapter 11 will complete the set.

— PNEUMA
